summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming. It then said outright that it was taking the **bounded** path, showed a short design in chat and edited app.js once I approved. It never wrote a spec document to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ or docs/superpowers/specs/. The escalation criteria fail.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 fail. The agent said outright it was taking the bounded path, which is the exact failure pattern criterion 4 describes. No spec file exists in the repo, and it started implementing right after I approved the in-chat design.

observations.description: Router misclassification: the agent itself noted that the task "changes `login`'s signature" (a public interface change) and still picked the bounded path because the flow sits "in one file". Seeing a signature change should have pushed it to the architectural path.

The design analysis itself was good. It questioned the premise (the client can't know a userId before auth), offered 4 options through AskUserQuestion and recommended putting userId in the return value instead of adding a parameter, which in the end avoided the signature change. Even so, the process skipped the spec document.
The agent flagged that persistence and analytics tracking were out of scope instead of quietly widening the work. That was good scoping communication.
On first launch, both the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs default to 'No, exit', so I had to press Down each time. This is Claude Code onboarding, not the plugin.

During implementation the agent wrote a verification harness to /tmp/verify-login.js, outside the repo and outside the per-run TMPDIR, and then deleted it. This is minor, but it ignores the TMPDIR it was given.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log (1efbce30-...jsonl): {"tool":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming",...}}. This came before the Edit calls.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/*/specs/ before asking for approval
criteria.evidence: The agent's text in the log: "it changes `login`'s signature ... so brainstorming, on the **bounded** path (the login flow already exists here, in one file). I'll present a short design in chat". Running `ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". `git status --short` shows only " M app.js" and git log has no new commits.

criteria.criterion: Spec doc presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: No spec doc was ever written or presented. The approval gate was an in-chat design headed "Short design" that ended "Does this look right? I'll implement once you say yes." After that the log shows Edit calls on app.js.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec doc
criteria.evidence: It said outright "on the **bounded** path ... I'll present a short design in chat", then gave the in-chat design with no spec file (no docs/ directory exists).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / propose a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: The classification was 'bounded', not spike, and no probe plan was shown. The only throwaway item was a /tmp/verify-login.js harness it wrote during implementation to verify the change.
